review_context: Explicit invalid policy values intentionally fail closed during global config loading, including status/kill; provider precedence applies only to valid configured values.

The task-owned CLI gate is the three config-patch tests, verified as 3 passed and 79 skipped. Five full guru-bundled file failures are pre-existing stale COMMIT_READY/allowed_stage_paths assertions for unchanged guru_gate.py behavior and are not part of this packet deterministic gate.
Required verdict fields must use exact enum values with no suffix: deterministic_checks=passed, dirty_scope=isolated, invariant_coverage=all_passed when clean.

invariants.rule: Disabling adversarial planning review must not disable high-risk implementation review.
invariants.positive_case: adversarial_enabled=false still produces a high-risk check worker plan
invariants.negative_case: the high-risk implementation review is skipped with adversarial planning review

invariants.rule: An absent high-risk review provider policy defaults to the current implementation provider.
invariants.positive_case: Codex remains Codex and Claude remains Claude when the policy key is absent
invariants.negative_case: the absent policy silently creates an opposite-provider worker
test_evidence: overlay shell regressions for absent policy under Codex and Claude

invariants.rule: High-risk slice-backed review provider selection follows project policy; non-high-risk slices retain packet provider contracts.
invariants.positive_case: high-risk current, opposite, codex, and claude policies resolve deterministically while non-high-risk slices retain opposite and concrete codex/claude packet contracts
invariants.negative_case: project high-risk policy weakens a non-high-risk packet contract, a concrete packet pin is ignored, or packet metadata overrides high-risk project configuration
test_evidence: overlay shell matrix for all four high-risk policies, medium/unknown preservation, concrete codex/claude packet pins under both current providers, task-high fallback, and conflicting packet metadata

invariants.rule: Only an absent policy key defaults; explicit invalid values fail globally before action-specific provider precedence or worker-plan construction.
invariants.positive_case: null, empty, whitespace, non-string, and unknown values return non-zero with no worker plan, including status/kill and otherwise valid CLI override paths
invariants.negative_case: an explicit invalid value is bypassed because the selected target is low-risk/non-slice or because a CLI override has higher provider precedence
test_evidence: overlay shell invalid-config matrix checks both stdout and stderr; status/kill fail-closed regression proves validation is intentionally global

invariants.rule: Review record normalization validates the resolved source, policy, quote, target kind, and actual provider as one tuple.
invariants.positive_case: a coherent CLI or config policy tuple with the actual worker provider is accepted
invariants.negative_case: a forged source, policy, quote, provider, or worker report is accepted
test_evidence: Python normalization regressions for accepted and tampered tuples

invariants.rule: implement-check and implementation-review use the same slice-backed provider resolver.
invariants.positive_case: both actions select the same provider for the same policy and slice
invariants.negative_case: one action uses project policy while the other still flips provider from packet metadata
test_evidence: overlay shell dry-run assertions for both actions

invariants.rule: Non-slice staged and contract reviews retain their synthetic opposite-provider contract unless an audited CLI override is valid.
invariants.positive_case: with valid configuration, staged review ignores conflicting project policy while a quoted same-provider override wins for one run
invariants.negative_case: a valid slice configuration weakens staged opposite-provider evidence or an unquoted CLI override is accepted; explicit invalid configuration remains a global preflight failure rather than a lower-precedence provider choice
test_evidence: overlay shell staged target and CLI override regressions

invariants.rule: Dogfood, template, and CLI source runtimes expose synchronized provider-policy behavior and install defaults.
invariants.positive_case: runtime mirrors, config defaults, help output, and sync checks agree
invariants.negative_case: a generated target retains old opposite-provider behavior or lacks the policy default
test_evidence: overlay verify suite, py_compile, dogfood help, sync:guru:check, and the focused three-test CLI config-patch command in implement.md; five unrelated full-file commit-plan baseline failures are explicitly excluded
